description:
The surah that opens with the command to highly exalt God, the Divine One who is **The Most Exalted**, far above all that is unworthy that people wrongly attribute to Him. It is named after "the Most Exalted" (al-aʿlā), mentioned in verse 1. The surah reassures the Prophet Muḥammad that God will help him and urging him to continue with his mission. The temporary nature of this world is highlighted through mention of the short life of green pasture (cf. verse 10:24 and verse 18: 45).
The surah is also known as Glory to Lord in the Highest, The Highest, The Most High

translations.1: _Celebrate_ the Name of _your_ Lord, the Most Exalted,
translations.5: then turned it into a black scum.
translations.6:
We shall have _you_ recite [the Qur'ān],
  then _you_ will not forget [any of it]
translations.7: except what Allah may wish. Indeed He knows the overt and what is hidden.
translations.8: We shall smooth _your_ way to [preach] the easiest [canon].
translations.9: So _admonish_, for admonition is indeed beneficial:
translations.10: he who fears will take admonition,
translations.11: and the most wretched will shun it
translations.12: —he who will enter the Great Fire,
translations.13: then neither live in it, nor die.
translations.14: Felicitous is he who purifies himself,
translations.15: celebrates the Name of his Lord, and prays.
translations.16: Rather you prefer the life of this world,
translations.17: while the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
translations.18: This is indeed in the former scriptures,
translations.19: the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
